column3: The Hebrew says do not hide Yourself from his plea; BSB says do not ignore it.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew describes hostility in anger; BSB describes reviling in anger.
The Hebrew describes the heart trembling and terrors falling upon him; BSB says the heart murmurs and terrors assail.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says settle or dwell; BSB says find rest.
The Hebrew explicitly names lodging overnight in the wilderness; BSB says remain.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew names dividing their tongue in the singular; BSB describes confusing and confounding their speech.
The Hebrew says they circle the city on its walls; BSB says they encircle the walls.
The Hebrew has a singular public square; BSB has streets.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew calls him an acquaintance as well as an intimate; BSB says companion and close friend.
The Hebrew locates walking in God’s house; BSB says walking into it.
The Hebrew also names evil within them; BSB describes evil with them in their homes.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew orders the times evening, morning, and noon; BSB says morning, noon, and night.
The Hebrew says many were with him without explicitly naming opposition; BSB says many oppose him.
The Hebrew uses wording of answering them; BSB says humiliating them.
The Hebrew leaves the singular actor unnamed and describes stretching out his hands; BSB names my companion and says attacks.
The Hebrew names creamy things of his mouth; BSB describes speech smooth as butter.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew names a well of the pit; BSB says Pit of destruction.
